newsitem.title: FRENCH POLYNESIA: Petrol bombs hit Tahiti barracks.
newsitem.headline: Petrol bombs hit Tahiti barracks.

text.p: Attackers hurled petrol bombs at three paramilitary gendarmerie barracks and a shop on the French Polynesian island of Tahiti on Wednesday but caused little damage, police said.
No one claimed responsibility for the attacks, which came just after a news conference in which separatist leaders denounced "French occupation" and called for civil disobedience.
The separatists were protesting against the trial of James Salmon, a separatist candidate defeated in this week's French parliamentary election.
Salmon will appear in court later this month charged with abusing police for refusing to show his identity documents to gendarmes who stopped his car.
Salmon said police were foreigners and had no right to see his documents. Police said he had not fastened his safety belt.
The separatist movement used violence in 1995 to protest at a series of nuclear tests in French Polynesia, an overseas territory of France.
